types.oie_definition: A type of occupation or career requiring specific skills and training.
types.embedding_query_text: Profession: A type of occupation or career requiring specific skills and training. Also called occupation, career, job, vocation.

chosen_type.label: Occupation
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org 'Occupation' class directly matches the definition and examples of a profession.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: ProfessionalService
candidates.comment: ProfessionalService is a LocalBusiness type for providers of specialized services. Also called expert service, specialized service. Examples: a legal service, an accounting service, a dental practice, an architectural firm. Distinct from Service, which is a broader concept of an intangible offering.

candidates.label: Specialty
candidates.comment: Any branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise, typically through significant study and effort. Also called area of expertise, specialization, discipline, field. Examples: 'Cardiology' as a medical specialty, 'Corporate Law' as a legal specialty, 'Artificial Intelligence' as a computer science specialty.

candidates.label: Certification
candidates.comment: An official and authoritative statement attesting to specific characteristics of a subject, issued by an independent body. Also called accreditation, credential, attestation, endorsement. Examples: ISO 9001 certification, Organic food certification, PMP certification, LEED certification.

candidates.label: Course
candidates.comment: A Course is a description of an educational program or curriculum designed to impart knowledge, competence, or ability to learners. Also called educational program, curriculum, study program, academic course. Examples: "Introduction to Python Programming," "Art History 101," "Advanced Calculus," "Yoga Teacher Training." Distinct from CourseInstance, which is a specific offering of a course at a particular time and place.

types.oie_definition: An official or honorary designation given to a person, often indicating achievement or status.
types.embedding_query_text: Title: An official or honorary designation given to a person, often indicating achievement or status. Also called designation, honor, award title, status.

chosen_type.label: HonoraryTitle
chosen_type.definition: An official or honorary designation given to a person, often indicating achievement or status.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org candidate accurately captures the specific meaning of an honorary designation or title, as opposed to a status, occupation, or document.

candidates.label: StatusEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration type representing various status types or states. Also called status list, state types, condition enumeration. Examples: 'Active', 'Pending', 'Completed', 'Cancelled'.

candidates.label: CertificationStatusEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration defining the possible statuses of a certification. Also called certification state, approval status, credential status. Examples: Active, Inactive, Expired, Pending.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: Certification
candidates.comment: An official and authoritative statement attesting to specific characteristics of a subject, issued by an independent body. Also called accreditation, credential, attestation, endorsement. Examples: ISO 9001 certification, Organic food certification, PMP certification, LEED certification.

candidates.label: Credential
candidates.comment: A Credential is a certificate or document used to verify the identity, qualifications, or authority of a person or entity. Also called certificate, qualification, accreditation, license, identification. Examples: A driver's license, a university degree, a professional certification, a digital security certificate.

types.oie_definition: A specific day of the calendar year.
types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific day of the calendar year. Also called calendar day, specific day.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org 'Date' data type is a direct and precise match for a specific calendar day.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

types.oie_definition: A type of bakery specializing in pastries and sweets.
types.embedding_query_text: Patisserie: A type of bakery specializing in pastries and sweets. Also called pastry shop, bakery, sweet shop.

chosen_type.label: Bakery
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org 'Bakery' class explicitly lists 'patisserie' as an alias and matches the definition.

candidates.label: Bakery
candidates.comment: A FoodEstablishment that bakes and sells bread, cakes, and pastries. Also called bake shop, patisserie, bread shop. Examples: "The Daily Bread Bakery", "Sweet Delights Patisserie", "Grandma's Oven".

candidates.label: IceCreamShop
candidates.comment: An IceCreamShop is a food establishment local business specializing in selling ice cream and related frozen desserts. Also called gelateria, ice cream parlor, frozen dessert shop. Examples: Baskin-Robbins, Ben & Jerry's Scoop Shop, a local artisanal ice cream store.

candidates.label: CafeOrCoffeeShop
candidates.comment: A CafeOrCoffeeShop is a FoodEstablishment primarily serving coffee, other beverages, and often light meals or pastries. Also called coffee house, coffee bar, cafe. Examples: Starbucks, local independent coffee shop, a small bistro. Distinct from Restaurant, which typically offers a wider range of full meals.

candidates.label: Florist
candidates.comment: A Florist is a Store that sells flowers and floral arrangements. Also called flower shop, floral designer. Examples: A local flower shop, an online florist delivering bouquets, a wedding floral specialist.

candidates.label: ConvenienceStore
candidates.comment: A local business retail store offering a limited range of everyday items, often with extended hours. Also called corner store, mini-mart, quick shop. Examples: 7-Eleven, Circle K, a local neighborhood market, a gas station store. Distinct from Store, which is a general retail establishment.

types.oie_definition: A large and permanent human settlement.
types.embedding_query_text: City: A large and permanent human settlement. Also called metropolis, town, urban area.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org 'City' class is a direct and precise match for a large human settlement.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

types.oie_definition: A phrase indicating a person's age.
types.embedding_query_text: Age Descriptor: A phrase indicating a person's age. Also called age indication, age phrase.

chosen_type.label: AgeDescription
chosen_type.definition: A phrase indicating a person's age.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org candidate specifically describes a phrase indicating a person's age; 'Duration' is too broad.

candidates.label: AdultOrientedEnumeration
candidates.comment: AdultOrientedEnumeration is an Enumeration of factors that make a product or content relevant or potentially restricted for adults only. Also called adult content classification, age restriction type, mature content indicator. Examples: `AdultSexualContent`, `ViolentContent`, `GamblingContent`.

candidates.label: PreventionIndication
candidates.comment: A PreventionIndication is a MedicalIndication for preventing an underlying medical condition, symptom, or disease. Also called prophylactic indication, preventative use. Examples: a vaccine for measles prevention, a medication to prevent migraines, dietary changes to prevent heart disease, exercise to prevent diabetes.

candidates.label: DrugPrescriptionStatus
candidates.comment: A DrugPrescriptionStatus is a MedicalEnumeration indicating whether a drug is available by prescription or over-the-counter. Also called medication availability, prescription requirement. Examples: PrescriptionOnly, OverTheCounter.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: MedicalIndication
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing a condition or factor that suggests the use of a medical therapy. Also called indication for treatment, therapeutic rationale, medical justification. Examples: "high blood pressure" as an indication for antihypertensive drugs, "fever" as an indication for antipyretics.

types.oie_definition: A distinguishing characteristic of a person's body or appearance.
types.embedding_query_text: Physical Trait: A distinguishing characteristic of a person's body or appearance. Also called physical characteristic, appearance feature.

chosen_type.label: SuperficialAnatomy
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org 'SuperficialAnatomy' class covers observable physical features and appearance.

candidates.label: SuperficialAnatomy
candidates.comment: Anatomical features observable by sight without dissection, including body form, proportions, and surface landmarks corresponding to deeper structures. Also called surface anatomy, external anatomy, visible body structures. Examples: the visible edges of the scapula, the cubital fossa for vein location, the contours of muscles under the skin.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

candidates.label: PhysicalActivity
candidates.comment: PhysicalActivity, as a LifestyleModification, is any bodily activity that enhances or maintains physical fitness and overall health. Also called exercise, workout, physical exertion. Examples: running, swimming, yoga, weightlifting. Distinct from MedicalTherapy, which is a treatment for a specific condition.

candidates.label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical condition representing any feature, objective or subjective, associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical manifestation, health indicator, disease feature. Examples: "pain", "fever", "fatigue", "rash", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is the underlying state itself.

candidates.label: AnatomicalStructure
candidates.comment: An AnatomicalStructure is a MedicalEntity representing any part of the human body, such as organs, tissues, or cells. Also called body part, biological structure, anatomical component. Examples: The heart, a bone, a muscle, a neuron, the liver. Distinct from AnatomicalSystem, which is a group of structures working together.

types.oie_definition: A structured group of people with a particular purpose.
types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people with a particular purpose. Also called association, institution, group, body.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org 'Organization' class is a direct and precise match for a structured group of people with a purpose.

mentions: International Union of Bakers and Confectioners (UIBC)

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

types.oie_definition: A prize or other mark of recognition given in honor of an achievement.
types.embedding_query_text: Award: A prize or other mark of recognition given in honor of an achievement. Also called prize, honor, recognition, trophy.

chosen_type.label: AchievementAward
chosen_type.definition: A prize or other mark of recognition given in honor of an achievement.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org candidate directly represents an 'Award' as a prize or recognition; 'Certification' is too formal and specific.

candidates.label: WinAction
candidates.comment: The act of achieving victory or success in a competitive activity. Also called triumph, succeed, prevail. Examples: winning a race, winning a championship, winning an argument.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: Certification
candidates.comment: An official and authoritative statement attesting to specific characteristics of a subject, issued by an independent body. Also called accreditation, credential, attestation, endorsement. Examples: ISO 9001 certification, Organic food certification, PMP certification, LEED certification.

types.oie_definition: A phrase that indicates a point or period in time, often relative to another event or the present.
types.embedding_query_text: Temporal Expression: A phrase that indicates a point or period in time, often relative to another event or the present. Also called time phrase, time reference, date reference.

chosen_type.label: RelativeTemporalExpression
chosen_type.definition: A phrase that indicates a point or period in time, often relative to another event or the present.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org candidate captures the relative and descriptive nature of these temporal phrases; 'Duration' is too absolute.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: SeekToAction
candidates.comment: The action of navigating to a specific timestamp within a video object, typically using a URL parameter. Also called jump to time, fast forward to, skip to, go to timestamp. Examples: clicking a link that starts a YouTube video at 2:30, using a video player's seek bar.

types.oie_definition: A business that sells goods directly to consumers.
types.embedding_query_text: Retail Establishment: A business that sells goods directly to consumers. Also called store, shop, boutique.

chosen_type.label: Store
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org 'Store' class is a direct and precise match for a retail business selling goods to consumers.

candidates.label: Store
candidates.comment: A retail business that sells goods to consumers. Also called shop, retail outlet, boutique, market. Examples: a grocery store, a clothing store, an electronics store, a bookstore.

candidates.label: WholesaleStore
candidates.comment: A local business that sells goods in large quantities, typically to retailers or other businesses, rather than directly to individual consumers. Also called wholesaler, bulk store, cash and carry. Examples: Costco Business Center, a restaurant supply store, a building materials wholesaler.

candidates.label: OutletStore
candidates.comment: An OutletStore is a local business that sells goods, often at reduced prices, directly from a manufacturer or retailer. Also called factory outlet, discount store, clearance store. Examples: a Nike outlet, a designer brand outlet, a retail chain's clearance center. Distinct from DepartmentStore, which sells a wide range of goods at regular prices.

candidates.label: BookStore
candidates.comment: A BookStore is a LocalBusiness that sells books and related merchandise. Also called book shop, bookseller, literary retailer. Examples: Barnes & Noble, local independent bookstore, Amazon Books.

candidates.label: ClothingStore
candidates.comment: A local business specializing in the retail sale of apparel and accessories. Also called apparel store, boutique, fashion shop, garment retailer. Examples: H&M, Zara, Nordstrom, a local boutique. Distinct from Store, which is a general retail establishment.

types.oie_definition: A place where business is conducted, such as a shop, office, or factory.
types.embedding_query_text: Business Establishment: A place where business is conducted, such as a shop, office, or factory. Also called enterprise, company, firm, venue.

chosen_type.label: LocalBusiness
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org 'LocalBusiness' class represents a physical business serving a local community, fitting the definition of a business establishment.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: Store
candidates.comment: A retail business that sells goods to consumers. Also called shop, retail outlet, boutique, market. Examples: a grocery store, a clothing store, an electronics store, a bookstore.

candidates.label: BusinessEvent
candidates.comment: A BusinessEvent is an Event related to commercial activities, such as conferences, trade shows, or corporate meetings. Also called corporate event, professional gathering, industry event. Examples: a sales conference, a product launch event, an annual shareholder meeting. Distinct from SocialEvent, which is for personal or recreational gatherings.

candidates.label: LocalBusiness
candidates.comment: A specific physical business or a branch of an organization that serves a local community. Also called local company, neighborhood business, regional enterprise. Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

types.oie_definition: An individual human being.
types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called individual, human, figure.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org 'Person' class is a direct and precise match for an individual human being.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: ProfilePage
candidates.comment: A ProfilePage is a WebPage dedicated to displaying information about a specific entity, such as a person or organization. Also called user profile, personal page, bio page. Examples: a LinkedIn profile, a social media user's page, an author's biography page, a company's "About Us" page.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

types.oie_definition: A large area of land that has particular characteristics.
types.embedding_query_text: Region: A large area of land that has particular characteristics. Also called area, territory, district, locale.

chosen_type.label: DefinedRegion
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org 'DefinedRegion' class covers geographic areas, including those defined by non-administrative criteria, fitting the mentions well.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: Continent
candidates.comment: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

types.oie_definition: A baked food item made from dough, often sweet and decorated.
types.embedding_query_text: Pastry: A baked food item made from dough, often sweet and decorated. Also called sweet baked good, confection, dessert item.

chosen_type.label: BakedPastry
chosen_type.definition: A baked food item made from dough, often sweet and decorated.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org candidate is specific enough for 'Pastry'; 'Product' is too general, and 'Bakery' is a business.

candidates.label: Bakery
candidates.comment: A FoodEstablishment that bakes and sells bread, cakes, and pastries. Also called bake shop, patisserie, bread shop. Examples: "The Daily Bread Bakery", "Sweet Delights Patisserie", "Grandma's Oven".

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: IceCreamShop
candidates.comment: An IceCreamShop is a food establishment local business specializing in selling ice cream and related frozen desserts. Also called gelateria, ice cream parlor, frozen dessert shop. Examples: Baskin-Robbins, Ben & Jerry's Scoop Shop, a local artisanal ice cream store.

candidates.label: CookAction
candidates.comment: The act of preparing or producing food through cooking processes. Also called cooking, food preparation, culinary action, baking. Examples: Baking a cake, frying an egg, grilling a steak, boiling pasta. Distinct from CreateAction, which is a broader category for making something.

candidates.label: FoodEvent
candidates.comment: A FoodEvent is an Event centered around food and drink. Also called culinary event, gastronomic event, food festival. Examples: A wine tasting, a cooking class, a food fair, a restaurant week promotion.

types.oie_definition: A small, flat, baked cake, typically crisp.
types.embedding_query_text: Biscuit: A small, flat, baked cake, typically crisp. Also called cookie, cracker, shortbread.

chosen_type.label: BakedBiscuit
chosen_type.definition: A small, flat, baked cake, typically crisp.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org candidate is specific enough for 'Biscuit'; 'Bakery' is a business, not the item itself.

candidates.label: Bakery
candidates.comment: A FoodEstablishment that bakes and sells bread, cakes, and pastries. Also called bake shop, patisserie, bread shop. Examples: "The Daily Bread Bakery", "Sweet Delights Patisserie", "Grandma's Oven".

candidates.label: ShortStory
candidates.comment: A brief work of literature, typically written in narrative prose, focusing on a single plot or theme. Also called tale, novelette, short fiction, narrative. Examples: Edgar Allan Poe's 'The Tell-Tale Heart', O. Henry's 'The Gift of the Magi', a story from a literary magazine.

candidates.label: FoodEstablishment
candidates.comment: A FoodEstablishment is a LocalBusiness primarily involved in food-related services. Also called eatery, restaurant, food service provider. Examples: A restaurant, a cafe, a bakery, a catering company.

candidates.label: RestrictedDiet
candidates.comment: A RestrictedDiet is an Enumeration representing a diet limited to certain foods or preparations due to cultural, religious, health, or lifestyle reasons. Also called special diet, dietary restriction. Examples: vegan diet, gluten-free diet, kosher diet, low-sodium diet.

candidates.label: BarOrPub
candidates.comment: A FoodEstablishment that primarily serves alcoholic beverages and often food. Also called bar, pub, tavern, lounge. Examples: "The Green Dragon Pub", "O'Malley's Bar & Grill", "The Corner Taproom". Distinct from Restaurant, which primarily focuses on serving meals.

types.oie_definition: A general category for any item intended for consumption as food.
types.embedding_query_text: Food Item: A general category for any item intended for consumption as food. Also called edible, foodstuff, provision.

chosen_type.label: MenuItem
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org 'MenuItem' class represents a single food or drink item, which fits the general concept of a food item.

candidates.label: DietarySupplement
candidates.comment: A product taken orally that contains dietary ingredients intended to supplement the diet, such as vitamins, minerals, or herbs. Also called Nutritional supplement, health supplement, vitamin, herbal remedy. Examples: Multivitamin pills, fish oil capsules, protein powder, ginseng extract. Distinct from Drug, which is primarily for treating, preventing, or diagnosing disease.

candidates.label: FoodService
candidates.comment: A FoodService is a Service related to providing food, such as breakfast, lunch, or dinner. Also called meal service, catering service, dining option. Examples: Breakfast service at a hotel, a school lunch program, an in-flight meal service, a catering package for an event.

candidates.label: EatAction
candidates.comment: EatAction is a ConsumeAction representing the act of swallowing solid objects. Also called consuming food, dining, ingesting. Examples: Eating a meal, consuming a snack, having dinner, biting into an apple.

candidates.label: MenuItem

types.oie_definition: The sweet course eaten at the end of a meal.
types.embedding_query_text: Dessert: The sweet course eaten at the end of a meal. Also called sweet course, pudding, afters.

candidates.label: CafeOrCoffeeShop
candidates.comment: A CafeOrCoffeeShop is a FoodEstablishment primarily serving coffee, other beverages, and often light meals or pastries. Also called coffee house, coffee bar, cafe. Examples: Starbucks, local independent coffee shop, a small bistro. Distinct from Restaurant, which typically offers a wider range of full meals.

candidates.label: Bakery
candidates.comment: A FoodEstablishment that bakes and sells bread, cakes, and pastries. Also called bake shop, patisserie, bread shop. Examples: "The Daily Bread Bakery", "Sweet Delights Patisserie", "Grandma's Oven".

candidates.label: IceCreamShop
candidates.comment: An IceCreamShop is a food establishment local business specializing in selling ice cream and related frozen desserts. Also called gelateria, ice cream parlor, frozen dessert shop. Examples: Baskin-Robbins, Ben & Jerry's Scoop Shop, a local artisanal ice cream store.

candidates.label: FoodService
candidates.comment: A FoodService is a Service related to providing food, such as breakfast, lunch, or dinner. Also called meal service, catering service, dining option. Examples: Breakfast service at a hotel, a school lunch program, an in-flight meal service, a catering package for an event.

candidates.label: FoodEvent
candidates.comment: A FoodEvent is an Event centered around food and drink. Also called culinary event, gastronomic event, food festival. Examples: A wine tasting, a cooking class, a food fair, a restaurant week promotion.

types.oie_definition: Each of the twelve divisions of the year.
types.embedding_query_text: Month: Each of the twelve divisions of the year. Also called calendar month.

chosen_type.label: Month
chosen_type.definition: Each of the twelve divisions of the year.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org candidate specifically represents a calendar month; 'Duration' is the closest suitable parent.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Periodical
candidates.comment: A Periodical, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a publication issued in successive parts with numerical or chronological designations, intended to continue indefinitely. Also called serial publication, magazine, journal. Examples: The New Yorker magazine, a scholarly journal, a daily newspaper. Distinct from Book, which is a single, non-serial publication.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.
